question: What, according to O'Neil, is a good test of whether a scoring model is fair?
options: People can see and contest it
answer: Whether the people it judges can see how it works and contest its mistakes, and whether its makers check its outcomes. O'Neil argues that a model without feedback never learns when it is wrong, while one open to appeal can be corrected. More data alone fixes nothing if the data is biased.
move: A fair model is one its subjects can question and its makers check.
trap: 'Lots of data': more data sounds more objective.
simply: A good teacher shows you how a test was marked so you can point out a mistake. A fair algorithm should do the same.
why: When an app or a company scores you, asking 'can I see why, and appeal?' is the most useful question you have.
